claims.explanation: AM-251 is a CB1/endocannabinoid receptor antagonist, and its selective killing likely reflects dependence on endocannabinoid/CB1 signaling for survival in a subset of tumor cells, particularly those with RAS/RAF-MAPK pathway activation and intact apoptotic signaling. Lines with BRAF, NRAS, KRAS, or MAP2K1 mutations are enriched among sensitive lines, whereas many resistant lines have alterations that may bypass this dependence (e.g., ALK fusions, NF2 loss, or PTEN/STK11 co-mutations). The virtual-cell response showing BCL2 upregulation and MAPK/FOXO-related changes is consistent with modulation of survival signaling rather than a general cytotoxic effect.

features.basis: Enriched in sensitive melanoma lines (K029AX, SH4, IGR37, LOXIMVI) and MAPK-driven survival dependence
Sensitive NCIH1299 and LOXIMVI carry NRAS alterations; RAS-MAPK activation may increase dependence on CB1/endocannabinoid signaling
Multiple sensitive lines (GSU_STOMACH, SNU410, SUIT2, HS766T) have KRAS mutations
Sensitive NCIH1437 has MAP2K1 mutation, implicating MAPK pathway activation
AM-251 targets CB1 (CNR1); high receptor expression may increase drug effect
AM-251 also targets GPR55; expression could mediate selective response
AM-251 annotated target; expression may contribute to sensitivity
PTEN mutations appear in several resistant lines (TE4, KALS1, FTC133, GP2D) and may reduce dependence on CB1-mediated apoptosis
Resistant lines TE4, KALS1 carry STK11 mutations, possibly bypassing metabolic stress
Resistant mesothelioma lines NCIH2052 and ISTMES2 have NF2 mutations
Resistant lines NCIH2452 and KELLY have ALK alterations, suggesting alternative survival signaling
Virtual cell shows BCL2 upregulation; high BCL2 may protect from AM-251-induced apoptosis
